Commentary.Commentary: Right, then! We are done with the formalities from this match. Afghanistan lead the 5-match series 2-0 and will play the next match to seal it right then and there. Zimbabwe must win anyhow to stay alive in the series. The 3rd match takes place on 21st February at 0930 local time (0730 GMT). Till then, take care!
Rashid Khan has been named the Man of the Match for his wonderful bowling performance. He finished with figures of 7.1-0-25-3.

Barring the initial assault laid on them by Solomon Mire, Afghanistan were right on the money with the ball. Almost all of their bowlers contributed with the wickets. Bowled tight lines, kept at it and eventually got the desired results. It was a collective, all-round performance which will please Asghar Stanikzai greatly. Earlier in the day, a couple of fifties from Shahzad and Shah, along with some solid hitting in the middle order from Nabi and Najibullah, saw Afghanistan post a total which proved to be too daunting for the home team.

So, that's it! Afghanistan win by 54 runs. A rather sad end to Zimbabwe's run chase, especially after the way they kicked things off. With 239 runs to chase, Solomon Mire got the hosts off to a blazing start. At a fast pace, he reached his fifty and then was quickly dismissed, but not before he set a good platform for his team. Then Craig Ervine and Ryan Burl took the reins, were playing sensibly, but the former just got out cheaply and from that point on, it was all downhill for them. Nobody managed to stick around as the opposition kept chipping at the wickets, and that proved to be their undoing.
OUT c Amir Hamza b Rashid Khan. Zimbabwe have been bowled out.
The end is nigh for Zimbabwe here...

After 40 overs, Zimbabwe have fallen into the abyss as the reel on 175/9. They have lost 3 wickets in Musakanda being stumped, Chatara getting bowled and Mpofu being caught at mid off. Nabi, Hamza and and then Nabi again doing the damage. Afghanistan are just 1 wicket away from victory here., they can almost taste it. Zimbabwe need 64 runs to win in 60 balls.
OUT c Rahmat Shah b Mohammad Nabi. Zimbabwe have lost their ninth wicket.
OUT b Amir Hamza. Zimbabwe have lost their eighth wicket.
OUT st Mohammad Shahzad b Mohammad Nabi. Zimbabwe have lost their seventh wicket.

After 35 overs, Zimbabwe have slipped to 157/6. The home side has lost 3 wickets and scored 27 runs. Craig Ervine was the first one to depart, then Ryan Burl followed soon after. Naib and Nabi the ones respectively to scalp their wickets. And then, after the two set batsmen were out of here, Amir Hamza got rid of Malcolm Waller, wasting no time. Afghanistan are in the driver's seat as of now and are primed for victory. Can Zimbabwe somehow manage to limp across the finish line? They need 82 to win from 90 balls. Or will the visiting team assert themselves even further?
OUT c & b Amir Hamza. Zimbabwe have lost their sixth wicket.
OUT b Mohammad Nabi. Zimbabwe have lost their fifth wicket.
OUT c sub b Gulbadin Naib. Zimbabwe have lost their fourth wicket.

After 30 overs, Zimbabwe have casually strolled on to 130/3. Some good new first up as the rain has stopped coming down. Craig Ervine and Ryan Burl have knocked the ball around and kept the scoreboard ticking. Adding 24 runs to their total, the hosts are comfortably going about their business. Been a rather tame period of play from the Afghans.

After 25 overs, adding 18 runs, Zimbabwe are 106/3. They've crossed the 100-run mark now with Craig Ervine and Ryan Burl looking solid. The rain however has picked up and the groundsmen are ready on the sidelines with the covers if it increases any more. Afghanistan are rushing through with the overs, trying to get the better of the DLS Method in case it rains. Play will continue... For the moment, at least.

After 20 overs, Zimbabwe have added 17 runs and lost 2 wickets as the scoreboard shows they are 88/3. Peter Moor and Hamilton Masakadza have walked back to the pavilion as Gulbadin Naib and Rashid Khan respectively have sent the two of them back. The visitors have crawled back into this game after the initial assault from Solomon Mire and have done well to get themselves into a good position now. An interesting phase of play awaits both teams.
OUT lbw b Rashid Khan. Zimbabwe have lost their third wicket.
OUT c Mohammad Shahzad b Gulbadin Naib. Zimbabwe have lost their second wicket.

After 15 overs, Zimbabwe have lost a wicket for 71 runs. The dangerous Solomon Mire has been dismissed as Afghanistan finally get a breakthrough. The leggie Rashid Khan bowled a real beaut and foxed Solomon with the wrong 'un, got it right through the gap between bat and pad to knock the bails over. The 71-run opening stand has been broken. Can the Afghans take advantage of this situation and make more inroads?
OUT b Rashid Khan. Zimbabwe have lost their first wicket.

After 10 overs, Zimbabwe have powered to 53/0 at the end of the first Powerplay. Solomon Mire is continuing with his onslaught and sending the ball to all parts of the Harare Sports Club. He's moved on to 43 off just 40 deliveries. Afghanistan don't know how to deal with him at the moment but Asghar Stanikzai is going to have to come up with something fast, otherwise this is not going to end well for him and his side.

After 5 overs, in contrast to Afghanistan, Zimbabwe have got off to a great start and motored to 30/0. And it's Solomon Mire who has taken charge of things. He's scored 25 of those 30 runs and is looking in good touch. Afghanistan need to vary things here and try a different plan, or else they're going to concede a lot of runs in this Powerplay from the looks of things.

Welcome back for the chase. It will be Solomon Mire and Peter Moor to lead the charge for Zimbabwe. Dawlat Zadran to take the new ball for Afghanistan. Unfortunately, due to lack of television feed, there won't be ball-by-ball commentary for this match but we shall keep you posted with updates.
